title: Induced category, fully faithful functor, essential image
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a category, let $C$ be a class (a type) and let $F:C\to\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$ be a function. The *induced category* $\mathcal D_F$ has as objects the elements of $C$, as morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_F}(x,y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(x),F(y))$, and the identities and the composition of $\mathcal D$. The *induced functor* $\iota_F:\mathcal D_F\to\mathcal D$ sends $x$ to $F(x)$ and is the identity on morphisms. A functor $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is *fully faithful* if every map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(G(x),G(y))$ is bijective; $\iota_F$ is fully faithful (its maps on morphisms are identities). The *essential image* of $G$ is the class of objects of $\mathcal B$ isomorphic to $G(x)$ for some object $x$ of $\mathcal A$; that of $\iota_F$ is the class of objects of $\mathcal D$ isomorphic to some $F(x)$. When $F$ is injective, $\mathcal D_F$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal D$ on the image of $F$.
